speaker: Unknown
en: So the thing that you need to think through is the risk of disruption.
zh: 所以你需要认真思考的问题是颠覆的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: What AI has done is massively increase the risk of disruptions.
zh: AI 所做的，是极大地增加了颠覆的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've had a challenging year this year with Lucy.
zh: 你今年和 Lucy 一起经历了艰难的一年。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happened?
zh: 发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, otherwise healthy child, what happened was she had, unbeknownst to us, what's called an arterial venous malformation, which is a kind of structure in the brain where the way the doctors describe it is the arteries, you know, typically blood flows into the arteries and then to the capillaries.
zh: 你知道，本来是个健康的孩子，发生的事情是，在我们不知情的情况下，她有一种叫做动静脉畸形的东西，这是大脑里的一种结构，医生是这样描述的：通常血液流入动脉，然后到毛细血管。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then to the veins.
zh: 然后再到静脉。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you go from arteries where there's a huge amount of blood flow to capillaries, the blood flow slows down, and then to the veins.
zh: 当你从血流量巨大的动脉进入毛细血管时，血流会减慢，然后到静脉。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in her case, she had like a bridge that went from the artery directly to the vein.
zh: 而在她的情况里，她有一条像桥一样的东西，直接从动脉连到静脉。

speaker: Unknown
en: So over time, there was too much pressure going into these veins in her brain, and one of those veins burst.
zh: 所以随着时间的推移，进入她大脑里这些静脉的压力过大，其中一条静脉破裂了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then a large amount of blood filled her brain, which is a confined volume.
zh: 然后大量血液充满她的大脑，而大脑是一个封闭的空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, it's a bit like a balloon blowing up inside your brain, and that put pressure on the surrounding brain and the skull, and obviously the skull doesn't move, so the pressure goes downward, it puts pressure on the midbrain.
zh: 所以，你知道，这有点像一个气球在你脑子里膨胀，对周围的大脑和头骨产生压力，显然头骨不会动，所以压力向下传导，压迫中脑。

speaker: Unknown
en: The midbrain is, you know, what keeps you breathing, keeps your heart beating.
zh: 中脑，你知道，是维持你呼吸、维持你心跳的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the really unfortunate thing, we believe this happened around nine in the morning, based on her orary.
zh: 而真正不幸的是，根据她的……我们相信这发生在早上九点左右。

speaker: Unknown
en: She lived, you know, young woman, lives alone in Williamsburg.
zh: 她一个人住在 Williamsburg，你知道，年轻女性，独自生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I texted her at four o'clock that day.
zh: 那天我四点钟给她发了短信。

speaker: Unknown
en: I had called her another time that day.
zh: 那天我还另外给她打过一次电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Other family members had done the same, but only when she hadn't picked up her luggage.
zh: 其他家人也做了同样的事，但只是在她没去取行李的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: She was, you know, she was leaving for Abu Dhabi for a wedding.
zh: 她，你知道，她当时正要去 Abu Dhabi 参加一场婚礼。

speaker: Unknown
en: A friend of hers was getting married the following day, and she was picking up her luggage from her mom's house.
zh: 她的一个朋友第二天要结婚，她要去她妈妈的房子取行李。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she didn't show when she was two hours late and no one could reach her that week.
zh: 当她迟到了两个小时、那个星期没人能联系上她的时候，她没有出现。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was sleeping at the time, but my oldest daughter went to find her and they found her lying.
zh: 我当时在睡觉，但我的大女儿去找她，她们发现她躺着。

speaker: Unknown
en: She found her lying on the floor of her apartment, barely breathing, you know, face down on the right side.
zh: 她发现她躺在公寓的地板上，几乎不能呼吸，你知道，脸朝下偏右侧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she thought she was dead.
zh: 她以为她死了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Called 911.

speaker: Unknown
en: She could hear her breathing in a very labored way.
zh: 她能听到她的呼吸非常费力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I don't sleep next to my cell phone.
zh: 而我睡觉时不把手机放在身边。

speaker: Unknown
en: My daughter doesn't know the landline number for my house.
zh: 我女儿不知道我家的座机号码。

speaker: Unknown
en: So she was able to call someone in the building.
zh: 所以她打电话给了楼里的某个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Guy in the building knocked on the door, pounded on the door, and handed me the phone with my daughter on, and then hopped in a cab.
zh: 楼里的一个男子敲门，用力砸门，把电话递给我，电话里是我女儿，然后他跳上了一辆出租车。

speaker: Unknown
en: The EMT didn't know which hospital to take her because they didn't know what had happened to her.
zh: 急救人员不知道该送她去哪家医院，因为他们不知道她出了什么事。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the big problems
zh: 其中一个大问题是

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes, you know, the EMT thinks someone's just drunk, and that's why they fell.
zh: 有时候，你知道，急救人员会以为某人只是喝醉了，所以他们摔倒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the way you treat a drunk person is you just let time go by, right?
zh: 而对待醉酒者的方式就是让时间过去，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Time going by for a person where the brain hemorrhage is very, you know, the more time the brain is under pressure, the more damage that can take place.
zh: 对于脑出血的人来说，时间的流逝非常，你知道，大脑受压的时间越长，可能造成的损伤就越大。

speaker: Unknown
en: Got to the hospital 1205, and she was just, you know, sitting on a gurney there while they were trying to figure out what she had.
zh: 12 点 05 分到达医院，她只是，你知道，坐在轮床上，而他们还在试图弄清她得了什么病。

speaker: Unknown
en: Eventually, they gave her a CT.
zh: 最终，他们给她做了 CT。

speaker: Unknown
en: They figured out she had a hemorrhage.
zh: 他们发现她有出血。

speaker: Unknown
en: They called the surgeon.
zh: 他们叫来了外科医生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what you need to do is you need to release the pressure on the brain as quickly as possible.
zh: 而你需要做的是尽快释放大脑的压力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the way you do that is you remove about 40% of the skull to allow the brain to expand beyond the skull.
zh: 你这样做的方式是移除大约 40% 的头骨，让大脑能够 expansion 到头骨之外。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we moved her from, you know, Elmhurst Hospital, by the way, very pleased with how they cared for her there, City Hospital in Queens.
zh: 我们把她从，你知道，Elmhurst 医院转走——顺便说一句，我们对他们在那里的照护非常满意——那是皇后区的市立医院。

speaker: Unknown
en: We moved her to Mount Sinai where, you know, Neary and I spent some time helping Mount Sinai, so we knew the team there.
zh: 我们把她转到了 Mount Sinai，你知道，Neary 和我曾在那里花时间帮助过 Mount Sinai，所以我们认识那里的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they also have very good neurosurgeons and a neuroscience brain practice.
zh: 而且他们有非常好的神经外科医生和神经科学脑科诊所。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, she was on a breathing tube.
zh: 而且，你知道，她当时插着呼吸管。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, she was wearing some bandage, of course, in her head, and it said, no bone, right, to make sure that nurses knew not to be careful.
zh: 你知道，她头上当然缠着一些绷带，上面写着，无骨，对，为了让护士知道不用小心。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's how we started.
zh: 我们就是这样开始的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I basically gave the doctors the dare to be great speech.
zh: 我基本上对医生们发表了「敢做伟业」的演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: I said, let's see what can be achieved by whatever you need from us, unlimited resources, let's look at latest and greatest technologies.
zh: 我说，让我们看看能取得什么成果，无论你们需要我们什么，无限的资源，让我们看看最新最好的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: They basically told us.
zh: 他们基本上告诉我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, look, Bill, we don't know what kind of deficit she's going to have.
zh: 你知道，听着，Bill，我们不知道她会有什么样的功能缺损。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, 19 hours of pressure on the brain.
zh: 你知道,19 个小时的大脑受压。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I didn't learn actually until weeks later.
zh: 你知道,其实我直到几周后才知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't normally do the surgery to save someone when it's been more than five hours because the assumption is brain death, basically.
zh: 他们通常不会在超过五个小时后做手术救人,因为基本假设是脑死亡了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So 19 hours, she's as close to death, you know, hours, minutes, I don't know exactly.
zh: 所以 19 个小时,她已经非常接近死亡,你知道,几小时,几分钟,我不确切知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we didn't know what would become of her, but I'm a very optimistic person.
zh: 所以我们不知道她会变成什么样,但我是一个非常乐观的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she's regained over time her cognition.
zh: 随着时间推移,她恢复了自己的认知能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's the same Lucy we knew.
zh: 她还是我们认识的那个 Lucy。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's got the same sense of humor.
zh: 她有同样的幽默感。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's really kind of remarkable.
zh: 她真的很了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: She woke up not being able to walk, to speak, and unfortunately to see.
zh: 她醒来时不能走路、不能说话,很遗憾,还不能看见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Her walking is coming back.
zh: 她的行走能力正在恢复。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think she's going to regain her ability to walk.
zh: 我认为她会重新获得行走的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Her speech very slowly is coming back.
zh: 她的语言能力恢复得非常缓慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's something like 17 vowels beyond the...
zh: 大概有 17 个元音,超出了……

speaker: Unknown
en: Vowels that we were taught.
zh: 超出我们以前学的那些元音。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she can do about 15 to the 17 now.
zh: 现在她能发大约 15 到 17 个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Each day, she's almost learning a new consonant.
zh: 每一天,她几乎都在学习一个新的辅音。

speaker: Unknown
en: She can say a few words.
zh: 她能说几个词了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Certainly, no, she's quite good at.
zh: 当然,「不」,她说得相当好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then vision, she's even shown some progress there.
zh: 然后是视觉,她在这方面也显示出一些进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I've spent a lot of time working with the doctors.
zh: 但我花了很多时间和医生们一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, my pitch to them was, let's see what we can do for her and everything we learned for her.
zh: 你知道,我对他们说的主张是,让我们看看能为她做什么,而我们为她学到的一切,

speaker: Unknown
en: We can help others.
zh: 我们可以用来帮助其他人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, Neri and I are going to make this available to everyone.
zh: 而且,你知道,Neri 和我会把这一切开放给所有人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And three months after, I guess, I was coming back from my birthday party and I got a call from a friend.
zh: 三个月后,我猜,我当时正从我的生日聚会回来,接到一个朋友的电话。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were talking to Mount Sinai, actually, about doing a redevelopment of their Fifth Avenue.
zh: 实际上,我们当时正在和 Mount Sinai 谈,重新开发他们在第五大道的

speaker: Unknown
en: campus to build a brain institute, some kind of brain center.
zh: 园区,建造一个大脑研究所,某种大脑中心。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had very aligned with our idea.
zh: 而他们的想法与我们的非常一致。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem with that is probably a 10-year project and super complicated, obviously taking down an existing hospital, moving people, bringing people back.
zh: 那个项目的问题在于,大概是一个 10 年的工程,而且超级复杂,显然要拆除一家现有的医院,转移人员,再把人迁回来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a vacant biotechnology building became available.
zh: 而这时一栋空置的生物技术大楼变得可买了。

speaker: Unknown
en: On 65th and 11th Avenue, 10 blocks from the office.
zh: 在第 65 街和第 11 大道,离办公室 10 个街区。

speaker: Unknown
en: And 60 days later, we closed in the building.
zh: 60 天后,我们完成了这栋楼的交割。

speaker: Unknown
en: We signed a contract to buy the rest of the site.
zh: 我们签了合同购买剩余的地块。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a 3.4-acre site.
zh: 那是一块 3.4 英亩的地。

speaker: Unknown
en: And our goal is to build the world's greatest brain institute.
zh: 而我们的目标是建造世界上最伟大的大脑研究所。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, everything from, you know, a focus on the patient.
zh: 你知道,一切从以患者为中心开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we get treatments to patients?
zh: 我们如何把治疗方法送到患者手中?

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's a ton of interesting things going on in technology.
zh: 而且科技领域正在发生大量有趣的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, everyone knows Neuralink.
zh: 显然,每个人都知道 Neuralink。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there are probably a dozen other companies working on brain-computer interfaces and other ways to get data from the brain, right?
zh: 但大概还有十几家其他公司在研究脑机接口,以及其他从大脑获取数据的方式,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, of course, AI, right?
zh: 而且,你知道,当然还有 AI,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: So not only are we able to get more and more data from the brain, we're able to interpret that data better than ever before.
zh: 所以,我们不仅能够从大脑获取越来越多的数据,我们还能比以往任何时候都更好地解读这些数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, I'm hoping Lucy can speak normally on her own, just working at it.
zh: 所以,你知道,我希望 Lucy 能靠自己的努力正常说话。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm hoping her vision returns, but if she has deficits in those areas, there will be solutions in the relative short to intermediate term.
zh: 我希望她的视力能恢复,但如果她在这些方面有缺陷,在相对中短期内会出现解决方案。

speaker: Unknown
en: Envision a world in where you wear a pair of glasses that basically have a camera, and the camera takes in the vision and ports it to your visual cortex, and that's how you see.
zh: 想象这样一个世界:你戴上一副基本上带有摄像头的眼镜,摄像头捕捉视觉信息并传输到你的视觉皮层,这就是你看东西的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: That will be how Elon says he's going to have a rudimentary way for people to see within a relatively short amount of time and within five years.
zh: Elon 说他将在相对短的时间内、五年之内,让人们拥有一种初步的视觉方式,将会是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've reached out to pretty much everyone for help on this, and he told me, he said, five years, well, people have better vision than bionic vision, in effect.
zh: 为了这件事,我几乎向所有人寻求过帮助,他告诉我,他说,五年,实际上,人们的视力会比仿生视觉更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way Dr. Kellner describes it to me is that there's been Lucy's lead on this whole thing.
zh: Kellner 医生向我描述的方式是,整个这件事一直是以 Lucy 为先导。

speaker: Unknown
en: Neurologists and even neurosurgeons or nihilists, they don't believe that the patients can make really material recoveries, and they can.
zh: 神经科医生,甚至神经外科医生,或者 nihilists,他们不相信患者能实现真正实质性的恢复,而他们可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've heard a lot of interesting stories of recovery, which are great to share with Lucy, but we're going to be able to do a lot more.
zh: 我们听到了很多有趣的康复故事,与 Lucy 分享这些很棒,但我们能做的会多得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: New York's actually probably one of the best places to do this, and there isn't anything like it.
zh: 纽约实际上可能是做这件事最好的地方之一，而且没有什么是像它这样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're excited about it.
zh: 我们对此感到兴奋。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you guys have done in response is just incredible.
zh: 你们所做出的回应真是令人难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so what's interesting is that all of the skills, experiences, relationships, resources that I've developed over my career work set me up to be incredibly well positioned to help my daughter.
zh: 是的，有意思的是，我在职业生涯中积累的所有技能、经验、人脉、资源，恰好让我处于一个非常有利的 position,能够帮助我的女儿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And to help other people that have this problem, right?
zh: 并帮助其他有这个问题的人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like a real estate investor, right?
zh: 我是一个房地产投资人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was able to buy the building, you know, at a fraction of what it cost.
zh: 所以我能够以远低于成本的一小部分价格买下这栋楼。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, architecture, design, also married to a very talented architect who's going to play a pretty important role here.
zh: 而且，建筑、设计方面，我还娶了一位非常有才华的建筑师，她将在这里扮演相当重要的角色。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think we're going to do something really interesting.
zh: 所以我觉得我们会做出一些非常有趣的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've had an incredible outpouring of people who want to be part of this, who, in many cases, we love people who write to us, you know, who've dealt with this on a very personal level, have a brother, a sister, a mother, a parent who've suffered, and they've seen kind of the nature of the treatment that's available today, and they want to change that.
zh: 而且我们收到了令人难以置信的大量人们表达想参与其中的意愿，很多情况下，我们喜欢那些给我们写信的人，他们曾在非常个人的层面上经历过这种事，有兄弟、姐妹、母亲、父母遭受过这种痛苦，他们见过当今可获得的治疗是什么样的，他们想改变这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's interesting, and actually, you know, people say, Bill, how do you deal with something like this?
zh: 这很有意思，实际上，你知道，人们说，Bill,你怎么应对这样的事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the first thing I had to do is figure out how to help my child.
zh: 嗯，我必须做的第一件事就是想办法帮助我的孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I made progress with that, this other thing is an amazing, you know, makes me feel like something good is coming out of, you know, I have this view that you, every bad thing, something good comes from it.
zh: 而当我在那方面取得进展时，这另一件事是一件了不起的，你知道，让我觉得有好的东西从中产生，你知道，我的看法是，每一件坏事，都会从中产生一些好的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, this is among the good that's coming from what she's going through.
zh: 你知道，这就是她正在经历的事情所带来的好的东西之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that makes me feel good.
zh: 这让我感觉很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you always have that view, or was that learned?
zh: 你一直都有这种看法吗，还是后来学到的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I figured that out over time.
zh: 我是随着时间慢慢想明白的。

speaker: Unknown
en: When?
zh: 什么时候？

speaker: Unknown
en: Was there a moment when that?
zh: 有没有那样的一个时刻？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, you know, I've had a few near-death experiences in business, and in each one of those cases, I was materially better off after that.
zh: 嗯，你知道，我在商业上经历过几次濒死的经历，而每一次那种情况下，我在那之后都实质上变得更好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are kind of, you know, good lessons.
zh: 所以那些算是，你知道，很好的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: The what does not kill you makes you a stronger thing is definitively true.
zh: 那句杀不死你的会让你更强大的话是确凿无疑的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, for my child, for Lucy, I think this is going to be good for her.
zh: 顺便说一句，对我的孩子，对 Lucy 来说，我认为这对她会是好事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Say more about that.
zh: 多说一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: Look, she's a wonderful, amazing person.
zh: 听着，她是一个美好、了不起的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you can recover from something as devastating as this, it's going to make her into like a superhuman person.
zh: 但如果你能从像这样毁灭性的事情中恢复过来，这会让她变成一个近乎超人的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she was, she is a wonderful human being.
zh: 而她曾经是，她现在是一个美好的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, one of the things that's helping her recover is, you know, one, you know, her mom has been there every day.
zh: 我是说，帮助她恢复的事情之一是，你知道，第一，她妈妈每天都在那里陪伴她。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I moved my office into the hospital.
zh: 你知道，我把我的办公室搬进了医院。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, within a day of her moving into the hospital, I did two IPOs, the two Pershing IPOs, I did from room 1107, room 107 on the 11th floor of 11 West at Mount Sinai Hospital, the power of Zoom.
zh: 你知道，在她搬进医院的一天之内，我完成了两次 IPO,就是那两次 Pershing 的 IPO,我是从 1107 房间，西 11 大楼 11 层的 107 房间，在西奈山医院完成的，Zoom 的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I would do a Zoom meeting for 45 minutes, and then I would go spend 15 minutes with my daughter.
zh: 所以我会开一个 45 分钟的 Zoom 会议，然后我去陪我女儿 15 分钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I'd do the next meeting.
zh: 然后我再开下一个会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I had my daughter as the inspiration, you know, for these two IPOs that we were working on.
zh: 所以我有我女儿作为这两次我们正在做的 IPO 的灵感来源，你知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we only moved her out of the hospital August 8th.
zh: 而且我们直到 8 月 8 日才把她移出医院。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she's been rehabilitating in Bridgehampton.
zh: 之后她一直在 Bridgehampton 康复。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then she's coming back into the city, you know, for a little procedure.
zh: 然后她要回城里，你知道，做一个小手术。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then she's moving into her own apartment that we've been, we bought an apartment in our building within a few weeks of the incident.
zh: 然后她将搬进她自己的公寓，我们在事发后几周内就在我们的大楼里买了一套公寓。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've been designing it to be
zh: 而且我们一直在设计它，使其成为

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the best rehab, recovery place for her to live.
zh: 你知道的，最适合她居住的康复、恢复之地。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, socialization, social interaction is absolutely critical for someone recovering from something like this.
zh: 你知道，社交化、社交互动对于一个从这样的事情中恢复的人来说绝对至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: The emotional support that you get and everything.
zh: 你能得到的情感支持和一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: And her friends have been amazing.
zh: 而她的朋友们一直非常了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Her friends have been with her every day.
zh: 她的朋友们每天都陪着她。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every day, one or more of her friends shows up and talks to her, eats with her and engages with her.
zh: 每天，都有她的一位或多位朋友出现，和她说话，和她一起吃饭，与她互动。

speaker: Unknown
en: And she's like this super giving person, ton of friends.
zh: 而她就是这种超级乐于付出的人，朋友很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone loves Lucy.
zh: 人人都爱 Lucy。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so she's getting an amazing return on that.
zh: 所以她正在从中获得惊人的回报，你知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, because her friends are showing up to save her.
zh: 你知道，因为她的朋友们都出现来拯救她。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of this makes me feel that humans can be so amazing.
zh: 所有这些让我觉得人类可以如此了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you know, you can recover from almost anything.
zh: 我是说，你知道，你几乎可以从任何事情中恢复过来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, there's a lot more hope for people who've had strokes, brain injuries, military TBI type stuff.
zh: 顺便说一下，那些经历过中风、脑损伤、军队那种创伤性脑损伤的人，其实还有很大的希望。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are a number of people in the field that have been really frustrated with how far we've not gone, who want to be the ones that fix this.
zh: 这个领域里有不少人一直对我们进展如此有限感到非常沮丧，他们想成为解决这个问题的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's been preventing us from going further?
zh: 是什么一直阻碍我们走得更远？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why haven't we pushed the limits on this stuff?
zh: 为什么我们一直没有在这些东西上突破极限？

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer is some combination of the insurance industry and just economics and hospitals, how they work.
zh: 答案是保险行业、经济因素和医院运作方式等几方面的组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, a neurosurgeon wants to do their surgery and then move on to the next one.
zh: 我是说，一个神经外科医生想做完他的手术，然后就去做下一台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Neurosurgeons are highly compensated, but they get paid for doing surgeries.
zh: 神经外科医生报酬很高，但他们的收入来自做手术。

speaker: Unknown
en: They don't get paid for the recovery of the patient over time.
zh: 病人随时间推移的康复，他们是拿不到钱的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know rehabilitation every hospital has some kind of rehabilitation program but in many cases it's embarrassingly inadequate and the insurance company might pay for only six weeks of care and then they get sent home and their home is you know not the ideal place and you and you need it's in a major takes a village.
zh: 你知道康复这件事，每家医院都有某种康复项目，但在很多情况下，其不足令人尴尬，保险公司可能只支付六周的护理费用，然后病人就被送回家，而他们的家你知道并不是理想的地方，而且你需要，这需要一个村子的人来支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: What if they're the principal breadwinner and they're devastated by this maybe the other family member has to go out and work as opposed to care for them.
zh: 如果他们是家里主要的经济支柱，被这事击垮了，也许另一个家庭成员就不得不出去工作，而不是照顾他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the most depressing things I was told by the head of rehab, actually a mass general we've been talking to, he said, Bill, what Lucy's achieved is remarkable.
zh: 我从康复科负责人那里听到过最令人沮丧的事情之一——其实是麻省总医院，我们一直在联系的——他说，Bill，Lucy 所取得的成就是非凡的。

speaker: Unknown
en: She's had incredible care.
zh: 她得到了极好的照护。

speaker: Unknown
en: The typical person, one, they wouldn't do the surgery.
zh: 普通人，第一，他们不会做那个手术。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two, if they do the surgery, the typical patient ends up in a nursing home when they check out of the hospital because the family can't take care of them, and they die a few months later from pneumonia because just the care that can be achieved in a nursing home.
zh: 第二，即使做了手术，典型的病人在出院时会住进养老院，因为家人无法照顾他们，几个月后死于肺炎，因为养老院能提供的护理就那样。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's super depressing.
zh: 这非常令人沮丧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so, you know, this is one of the cases where, you know, I'm financially unconstrained in my ability to help her, and so we can maximize the care.
zh: 所以，你知道，这是那种，你知道，我在帮助她的能力上不受财务限制的情况，所以我们可以把照护最大化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, what we're going to try to figure out in the institute is how we do this in a way that everyone can have the benefit of the care.
zh: 现在，我们在这个研究院要弄清楚的是，如何以一种让每个人都能享受到这种照护好处的的方式来做到这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Technology is going to help a lot.
zh: 技术会帮很大的忙。

speaker: Unknown
en: A great speech therapist could be $500 an hour.
zh: 一位优秀的言语治疗师可能每小时要 500 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: That, you know, insurance will pay for whatever percentage of that, but only for some period of time.
zh: 这个，你知道，保险会支付其中一定比例，但只在某段时间内。

speaker: Unknown
en: But people can keep recovering years and years later.
zh: 但人们在多年之后仍然可以持续恢复。

speaker: Unknown
en: But of course, AI could be an amazing speech therapist.
zh: 当然，AI 可以成为一名出色的言语治疗师。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there are lots of ways that technology are going to enable us to help people recover from these injuries.
zh: 所以有很多方式，技术将使我们能够帮助人们从这些损伤中恢复。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by the way, this all, you know, we're calling it, the focus is brain rehab recovery and longevity, right?
zh: 顺便说一下，这一切，你知道，我们称之为，重点是脑部康复恢复与长寿，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: What does a brain rehab recovery institute do?
zh: 一个脑部康复恢复研究院是做什么的？

speaker: Unknown
en: It focuses on brain recovery and your physical recovery.
zh: 它专注于大脑恢复和你的身体恢复。

speaker: Unknown
en: The brain plus your physical recovery is fundamentally longevity.
zh: 大脑加上你的身体恢复，从根本上说就是长寿。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other thing that hospitals aren't very good at,
zh: 还有另一件医院不太擅长的事，

speaker: Unknown
en: is nutrition, right?
zh: 就是营养，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: The food in hospitals is frightening, right?
zh: 医院里的食物很吓人，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: They have someone who has a, you know, heart attack, and the next morning they're having like pancakes with syrup with orange juice.
zh: 有人心脏病发作，第二天早上他们吃的是像浇了糖浆的煎饼配橙汁。

speaker: Unknown
en: In Lucy's case, you know, we made food for her for every meal.
zh: 在 Lucy 的情况下，你知道，我们为她每一餐都亲手做食物。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Institute's going to have amazing food because nutrition is critical.
zh: 这个研究院会有很棒的食物，因为营养至关重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are a lot of things we can do taking advantage of this financial circumstance.
zh: 利用这种财务条件，我们可以做很多事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to use it in a way that will enable us to build something optimal and I think ultimately self-sustaining.
zh: 我会以一种让我们能构建最优的、而且我认为最终能自我持续的东西的方式来使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're an incredible father.
zh: 你是一位了不起的父亲。

speaker: Unknown
en: What an amazing response to terrible circumstances.
zh: 对糟糕的境遇这是多么了不起的回应。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I would feel if I couldn't do it, I would be one of the most frustrated people in the world.
zh: 你知道，如果我不能做到，我会是世界上最沮丧的人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: I literally feel like I was designed to help her, like everything I knew how to do.
zh: 我真的觉得我就是被设计来帮助她的，就像我所知道的一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned the aura ring, the data on the aura ring.
zh: 你提到了 aura ring，aura ring 上的数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was the data that indicated something was?
zh: 是什么数据表明出了什么问题？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've been in touch with the CEO.
zh: 我一直和 CEO 保持联系。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've already actually reached out on Twitter.
zh: 我实际上已经在 Twitter 上联系过了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you can, certainly with an Apple Watch and hopefully with an Oura Ring.
zh: 而且我认为，用 Apple Watch 肯定可以，希望用 Oura Ring 也可以。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what happened was, if you look at her spike, I actually put it on Twitter, at like nine o'clock or so, there was a very quick spike in her pulse and then kind of a drop-off that looked kind of unusual.
zh: 情况是这样的，如果你看她的峰值，我实际上把它发在 Twitter 上了，在大约九点钟左右，她的脉搏出现了一个非常快速的飙升，然后有一种看起来挺不寻常的回落。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you combine that spike and a drop-off with someone falling, like the Apple Watch has an alert when someone falls.
zh: 如果你把这个飙升和回落与某人摔倒结合起来——就像 Apple Watch 有摔倒报警功能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, if that happens and it happens when there's a huge spike and they're- You can reasonably assume.
zh: 那么，如果这种情况发生了，而且发生时有一个巨大的飙升，而且他们——你可以合理地推断。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can say, did they have a heart attack?
zh: 你可以说，他们是不是心脏病发作了？

speaker: Unknown
en: Did they have a whatever?
zh: 他们是不是这样那样了？

speaker: Unknown
en: These are things you can look at.
zh: 这些都是你可以查看的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Oral Ring should have the same capability.
zh: 我认为 Oral Ring 应该具备同样的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they're working on it.
zh: 我想他们正在做这方面的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you keep your mind in a healthy place?
zh: 你如何让自己的心态保持健康？

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you do to keep your head right?
zh: 你做什么来保持头脑清醒？

speaker: Unknown
en: I play tennis almost every morning or do some form of exercise.
zh: 我几乎每天早上都打网球，或者做某种形式的锻炼。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's probably the most important thing I do because it's the one thing I do over the course of the day where I'm completely focused on the ball that's coming at me as opposed to whatever else is going on.
zh: 我想这可能是我做的最重要的事情，因为这是我一天当中唯一完全专注于朝我飞来的球的事情，而不是其他正在发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that is a really important form of meditation for me.
zh: 所以我认为这对我来说是一种非常重要的冥想形式。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's one.
zh: 这是一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got a good night's sleep.
zh: 我是说，你有四个实际上的公众实体。

speaker: Unknown
en: I spend time with my family, things like that.
zh: 我花时间陪家人，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you still meditate?
zh: 你还冥想吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I haven't in a while.
zh: 我有一阵子没冥想了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I did for this challenging year.
zh: 在这艰难的一年里我冥想过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I was in the middle of divorce.
zh: 当时我正在经历离婚。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was kind of on my own.
zh: 我差不多是一个人在撑着。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it really helped.
zh: 冥想真的很有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I probably should find 20 minutes a day to meditate.
zh: 我大概应该每天找出 20 分钟来冥想。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you manage it all?
zh: 你是如何管理这一切的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, you have four effective public entities.
zh: 我的意思是,你有四个实际上的公共实体。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have this with your daughter.
zh: 你和你女儿有这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have a seven-year-old.
zh: 你有一个七岁的孩子。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to be a great husband.
zh: 你想成为一个好丈夫。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you harmonize all of these things?
zh: 你如何协调所有这些事情？

speaker: Unknown
en: Pershing Square has come a long way from when I started it.
zh: Pershing Square 从我创立它以来已经走了很长的路。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I started it, I was sort of the chief bottle washer guy.
zh: 我创立它的时候，我差不多是那个打杂的头儿。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would come up with all the ideas, and I have an analyst that would help me prosecute them.
zh: 我会想出所有的点子，我有一位分析师帮我执行它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was activism, I was the guy, etc.
zh: 有激进投资的时候，我就是那个人，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Over 22 years, we've built an amazing team.
zh: 经过 22 年，我们打造了一支出色的团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're in an industry where the half-life of someone who works for a firm, you know, people are paying, you know, the top people can move from one place to another and get huge, you know, $100 million bonuses for showing up, things like this.
zh: 我们所处的行业里，为一个公司工作的人的半衰期，你知道，人们在付钱，你知道，顶层的人可以从一个地方跳到另一个地方，仅仅露面就能拿到巨大的、你知道的，1 亿美元的奖金，诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the result is a lot of turnover in the industry.
zh: 结果就是这个行业里人员流动很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have no turnover at Pershing Square.
zh: 我们在 Pershing Square 没有人员流动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that good or bad?
zh: 那是好还是坏？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, if there's someone that we've, you know, we've had no turnover.
zh: 嗯，如果说有某个人，你知道，我们没有人员流动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, we've made some mistakes and we've replaced some people over time.
zh: 显然，我们犯过一些错误，随着时间推移也替换过一些人。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you look at the investment team, the investment team has been the same team for now nine years with a couple of new additions.
zh: 但如果你看投资团队，投资团队到现在九年都是同一个团队，只有几个新加入的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's actually a really good thing.
zh: 而这实际上是一件非常好的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you have a constant revolving door with new people, you don't really know that you can trust people over time.
zh: 如果你有一个不断有人进出的旋转门，你无法真正知道随着时间推移你是否能信任这些人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they really telling you the truth?
zh: 他们是不是真的在跟你说实话？

speaker: Unknown
en: Are they really telling you all the risks and rewards of a particular situation?
zh: 他们是不是真的把某个特定情况的所有风险和回报都告诉你了？

speaker: Unknown
en: When you've built a relationship with people and you work with them for nine years and you have this culture of transparency and candidness, I don't for a second ever question anything that's being told to me by a member of the investment team.
zh: 当你和人们建立了关系，你和他们共事了九年，你们拥有这种透明和坦率的文化，我一刻也不会质疑投资团队任何成员告诉我的任何事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're telling me the flat, candid truth.
zh: 他们告诉我的是平实、坦率的真相。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a very comfortable place.
zh: 那是一种非常让人安心的状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: The answer to your question is the Pershing investment process is incredibly well run by a very experienced team that I play an important role in at the ultimate say, but I am no longer the guy that generates the bulk of the ideas.
zh: 对你问题的回答是，Pershing 的投资流程由一支非常有经验的团队运营得极其出色，我在其中扮演重要角色并拥有最终决定权，但我不再是那个产生大部分点子的人了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm someone that generates a minority of the ideas in the portfolio, so that's helpful.
zh: 我是在投资组合中产生少数点子的人，所以这很有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then the business itself, the way it's structured is Ben is responsible for running a lot of the business elements of Pershing Square.
zh: 然后是业务本身，它的结构方式是 Ben 负责运营 Pershing Square 的许多业务要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that frees me up to think.
zh: 所以这让我有空去思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: It frees me up to work on more strategic stuff, and it frees me up to come up with the occasional, you know, kind of idea.
zh: 这让我有空去做更多战略性的工作，也让我有空偶尔想出，你知道，那种点子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Pershing kind of takes care of itself.
zh: 所以 Pershing 基本上是自我运转的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we have a number of public entities.
zh: 嗯，我们有好几家上市公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have an amazing accounting team.
zh: 我们有一个很出色的会计团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, those public companies all sort of do the same thing.
zh: 而且，你知道，那些上市公司基本上都在做同样的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're really just...
zh: 它们其实只是……

speaker: Unknown
en: There's the management company that earns fees from the entities we're on, that's Pershing Square, Inc., PS, ticker.
zh: 有一家管理公司，从我们持股的实体那里赚取费用，那就是 Pershing Square, Inc.,股票代码 PS。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are two funds that are publicly traded that own effectively the same portfolio.
zh: 有两只公开交易的基金，它们持有的实际上几乎是同一个投资组合。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are certain governance responsibilities we have for those entities, but they're really actually, each of them have independent boards of directors.
zh: 团队拥有另外——

speaker: Unknown
en: So our role there is as the external investment manager.
zh: 他们不会同时在，你知道，其他 50 个董事会任职，所以我们有真正好的董事会。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have excellent boards at both of those.
zh: 这两家的董事会都非常优秀。

speaker: Unknown
en: The typical closed-end fund board is a bit of an embarrassment.
zh: 典型的封闭式基金董事会是有点丢人的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know how closely you follow the space, but you've seen Boas Weinstein going into proxy conference.
zh: 我不知道你对这个领域关注得有多紧，但你见过 Boas Weinstein 打代理权争夺战(proxy conference)。

speaker: Unknown
en: The typical closed-end fund board is a group of people who, I don't want to pick any, let's say BlackRock for the moment.
zh: 典型的封闭式基金董事会是一群这样的人，我不想点名，那就暂时说 BlackRock 吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I read somewhere that they sit on 86, the same six directors sit on 86 closed-end fund boards.
zh: 我记得在什么地方读到过，同样这六位董事在 86 家封闭式基金董事会任职。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard to do real governance when you sit on 86 boards of directors, right?
zh: 当你在 86 个董事会任职时，很难做真正的治理，对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: The typical limitation is four, you know, by ISS.
zh: 按 ISS 的标准，通常的上限是四家，你知道的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We hired actually real directors.
zh: 我们雇的是真正的董事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We pay them like real directors.
zh: 我们给他们真正的董事级别的报酬。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not serving on multiple, you know, 50 other, so we have really good boards.
zh: 他们没有在多个,你知道,其他 50 个……所以我们有非常好的董事会。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we do is fundamentally simple.
zh: 我们做的事从根本上说很简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pershing runs itself to some degree just because of delegation, incentives, alignment.
zh: Pershing 在某种程度上是自我运转的，靠的是授权、激励、一致性。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have the best alignment because no one's paid on individual stocks or based on performance.
zh: 我们有最好的一致性，因为没有人按单只股票或基于业绩获得报酬。

speaker: Unknown
en: At the end of the day, performance is going to be the biggest driver of our management company because the compounding of the underlying assets is what grows our fee stream.
zh: 归根结底，业绩仍将是我们管理公司最大的驱动因素，因为底层资产的复利增长才是我们费用流的增长来源。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just a very aligned entity.
zh: 这就是一个一致性极强的实体。

speaker: Unknown
en: I own about 45% of the company.
zh: 我拥有公司大约 45% 的股份。

speaker: Unknown
en: The team owns another.
zh: 团队拥有另一个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think 35% of the company and then we have a minority interest held by the public and some strategic investors that invest with us.
zh: 我想是 35% 的股份，然后还有少数股权由公众持有，以及一些和我们一起投资的战略投资者。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you get the alignment right, you get the people right, and you've got some principles written on a stone tablet and you've been doing it for a while.
zh: 如果你把一致性做对了，把人选对了，并且把一些原则写在石板上，而且你已经这么做了有一段时间了——

speaker: Unknown
en: But you're super competitive.
zh: 但你超级有竞争心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know.
zh: 我知道。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to be the best investor in the world.
zh: 你想成为世界上最优秀的投资者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is like one path, and then there's another path that's like dad and husband.
zh: 这就像是一条路，然后还有另一条路，就是父亲和丈夫。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would say the one thing I would say in the last, the setup of this AOI thing has consumed some mind share.
zh: 我想说的是，在过去——AOI 这个项目的搭建占用了我的心力份额。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of mine, as you would expect over the last 60 or 90 days because I'm assembling the team.
zh: 我的，正如你所预期的，在过去 60 或 90 天里，因为我正在组建团队。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like with, you know, there's a moment, it's a bit like we were at a proxy contest, we took control of a board of directors, now we've got to bring in a new CEO.
zh: 就像，你知道的，有一个时刻，有点像我们在打代理权争夺战，我们夺取了一家董事会的控制权，现在我们得引入一位新 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once we bring in the CEO and the teams in place and announced and everything else, I don't get involved in the day-to-day operations.
zh: 一旦我们引入了 CEO、团队到位并宣布完毕以及其他一切，我就不参与日常运营了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the same thing is going to be true for the AOI.
zh: AOI 也会是同样的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be like another portfolio company in some sense.
zh: 在某种意义上，它会像是又一个投资组合公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Although, you know, we're all going to sit on the board, you know, I'm going to chair the board.
zh: 不过，你知道，我们都会进入董事会，你知道，我会担任董事长。

speaker: Unknown
en: But there is a, you know, it is similar to, I don't think I could be doing, setting up the AOI, and we had a proxy contest underway at the same time.
zh: 但是有一个，你知道的，它确实类似于——我不觉得我能一边搭建 AOI,一边同时进行一场代理权争夺战。

speaker: Unknown
en: AOI is the Ackman, Ackman Institute, just for everybody listening.
zh: AOI 就是 Ackman,Ackman Institute,给所有在听的观众说明一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every few years, a new platform earns its place at the top of every smart advertiser's media plan.
zh: 每隔几年，就会有一个新平台在每个聪明广告主的媒体投放计划中赢得头把交椅。

speaker: Unknown
en: The people who find it early build advantages that are very hard to close.
zh: 那些早早发现它的人建立起了很难被追赶的优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: AppLovin just had the most remarkable run in ad tech history, and now they've opened that engine to businesses like yours.
zh: AppLovin 刚刚创造了广告技术历史上最了不起的一段历程，现在他们把那台引擎开放给了像你这样的企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Over a billion people play mobile games every day, focused, not scrolling, with no feed competing for their attention.
zh: 每天有超过十亿人玩手游，他们专注投入，不是在刷信息流，没有信息流来争夺他们的注意力。

speaker: Unknown
en: AppLovin puts your brand in front of the right customers and optimizes purely for your growth.
zh: AppLovin 把你的品牌呈现在正确的客户面前，并纯粹为你的增长做优化。

speaker: Unknown
en: Brands like Wayfair, Kitsch, Ridge, and Nectar are already scaling on it while most of their competitors don't even know it exists.
zh: Wayfair、Kitsch、Ridge、Nectar 这些品牌已经在它上面扩张了,而他们的大多数竞争对手甚至不知道它的存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ready to find your next million customers?
zh: 准备好寻找你的下一百万个客户了吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to applovin.com slash Shane and launch your first campaign today.
zh: 访问 applovin.com/shane,今天就启动你的第一个营销活动。

speaker: Unknown
en: I built an AI version of myself with Heijeng.
zh: 我用 Heijeng 建了一个我自己的 AI 版本。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you're about to see in here is my digital avatar.
zh: 你即将在这里看到的是我的数字化身。

speaker: Unknown
en: I asked it why some professionals build an audience while most stay invisible.
zh: 我问它,为什么有些专业人士能建立起受众,而大多数人却始终隐身。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here's what it said.
zh: 以下是它的回答。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, Shane, the professionals breaking out right now aren't the most talented ones.
zh: 嘿,Shane,现在突围而出的专业人士并不是最有才华的那些人。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're the most visible ones.
zh: 而是最有曝光度的那些人。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's their edge.
zh: 那就是他们的优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: They show up on video constantly, and nobody else can keep the pace.
zh: 他们持续不断地出现在视频里,而没有别人能跟得上这个节奏。

speaker: Unknown
en: Record yourself once, and I close that gap, so you become the face people trust.
zh: 你只要录一次自己,我就能弥合这个差距,让你成为人们信任的那张脸。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's HeyGen.
zh: 这就是 HeyGen。

speaker: Unknown
en: Record yourself for 15 seconds and get an avatar that keeps you posting without filming, so you don't need to become a full-time content creator.
zh: 录 15 秒自己的视频,得到一个让你无需拍摄也能持续发布内容的化身,这样你就不必成为全职内容创作者。

speaker: Unknown
en: 30 million people already use it, from financial advisors and real estate agents to 85% of the portion 100.
zh: 已经有 3000 万人在用它,从理财顾问、房产经纪人到 portion 100 的 85%。

speaker: Unknown
en: Your first three videos are free at heygen.com slash TKP.
zh: 你的前三条视频在 heygen.com/TKP 免费获取。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's H-E-Y-G-E-N dot com slash TKP.
zh: 也就是 H-E-Y-G-E-N dot com slash TKP。

speaker: Unknown
en: When do you do your best thinking?
zh: 你什么时候思维最活跃?

speaker: Unknown
en: Often it's when I'm on vacation, actually.
zh: 通常其实是我在度假的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of my best ideas are ones where I'm literally totally relaxed or I'm in the shower.
zh: 我最好的一些想法,都是在我完全放松的时候,或者在洗澡的时候。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've done a lot of research about bubbles.
zh: 你对泡沫做过很多研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm curious, like, how would you explain what a bubble is?
zh: 我很好奇,你会怎么解释什么是泡沫?

speaker: Unknown
en: A bubble is when human nature, when a lot of money is being made and people have a lot of FOMO and they want to participate in having money being made and it leads more and more money going into the same trade, if you will, until overvaluation takes place.
zh: 泡沫就是,当人性——当很多人在赚钱,人们有很多 FOMO(错失恐惧),他们想参与赚钱,这导致越来越多的钱进入同一笔交易,可以说,直到估值过高发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then, you know, ebullience and then eventually the bubble bursts.
zh: 然后,你知道,狂热沸腾,最终泡沫破裂。

speaker: Unknown
en: They seem to happen around these technological changes like railroads, automobiles, transistors, the internet.
zh: 它们似乎总是发生在这些技术变革周围,比如铁路、汽车、晶体管、互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are we in one now?
zh: 我们现在正处于一个泡沫中吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, we're certainly in a transition.
zh: 嗯,我们当然处于一个转型期。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could say AI is absolutely transformational and it's the most transformational technology I think of all of our respective lifetimes.
zh: 你可以说 AI 绝对是变革性的,而且我认为它是我们各自一生中最具变革性的技术。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are bubble-like elements.
zh: 存在类似泡沫的元素。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of crazy stuff going on, you know, in the private.
zh: 你知道,在私募领域有很多疯狂的事情在发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're starting to invest in some ... Talk about a bubble where Pershing is now investing in some venture-stage businesses.
zh: 我们开始投资一些……说到泡沫,Pershing 现在正在投资一些风险投资阶段的企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: Met with a company, let's say, two weeks ago, and they weren't raising money.
zh: 比如说,两周前见了一家公司,他们并没有在融资。

speaker: Unknown
en: Two days later, they close around.
zh: 两天后,他们完成了融资轮。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were preempted by some investor who put $50 million in at a $400 billion valuation.
zh: 他们被某个投资者抢先了,后者以 4000 亿美元的估值投了 5000 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then two weeks later, they raised another $50 million at a billion-dollar valuation.
zh: 然后两周后,他们又以十亿美元的估值融了 5000 万美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of people fearing missing out on
zh: 有很多人害怕错失

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, the future.
zh: 你知道,未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of capital going into venture, a lot of competition and a lot of preempting and leading to very high valuations.
zh: 所以大量资本涌入风险投资,大量竞争,大量抢先投资,导致非常高的估值。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I saw a company, you know, Series A round at a five billion pre-money.
zh: 你知道,我看到一家公司,A 轮融资,投前估值 50 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you avoid that FOMO?
zh: 你如何避免那种 FOMO?

speaker: Unknown
en: It depends on what you, where you are in life.
zh: 这取决于你处于人生的哪个阶段。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, Warren Buffett was remarkable for his discipline over a 60-year career.
zh: 你知道,Warren Buffett 在 60 年的职业生涯中,他的自律是非凡的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Actually, interestingly, in the last real bubble, the internet bubble, that's when Berkshire stock hit an all-time low because people said he's lost it.
zh: 实际上,有趣的是,在上一次真正的泡沫——互联网泡沫期间,那正是 Berkshire 股票创历史新低的时候,因为人们说他已经不行了。

speaker: Unknown
en: While all these other people are making money, he just didn't participate, but he just shouldered on.
zh: 当所有其他人都在赚钱时,他就是不参与,但他就是坚持挺了过去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's a question of short-term versus long-term perspective.
zh: 我认为这是短期视角与长期视角的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: What advice would you give founders right now who might be trying to raise?
zh: 你会给现在可能正在融资的创始人什么建议?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a great time to raise capital.
zh: 现在是融资的好时机。

speaker: Unknown
en: And assuming you raise the capital, don't spend it so quickly expecting money will be there forever.
zh: 而且假设你融到了资,不要花得太快,以为钱会永远在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: What this is reminiscent of is in the internet bubble, there was effectively unlimited amount of capital available for kind of suspect business plans.
zh: 这让人联想到互联网泡沫时期,当时实际上有无限量的资本可供那种可疑的商业计划书使用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there was a piece in Barron's one weekend and it listed all of the internet companies in the public markets and how much cash they had left.
zh: 然后有一个周末《巴伦周刊》上有一篇文章，列出了所有公开市场的互联网公司以及它们还剩多少现金。

speaker: Unknown
en: Based on kind of their burn rate, how many months to go before they went to zero.
zh: 根据它们的烧钱速度，还有多少个月会归零。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was probably the week before the market blew up.
zh: 那大概是市场崩盘前的一周。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happens to a private company that has no capital is a certain discipline associated with bootstrapping yourself.
zh: 一家没有资本的私营公司会发生什么，就是与自力更生相关的某种纪律。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you take in 50 million or 100 million and you completely change the way you deploy capital.
zh: 而当你拿到 5000 万或 1 亿美元时，你就完全改变了部署资本的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Betting that anytime you need money, you could just tap the markets.
zh: 赌的是任何时候你需要钱，你都可以直接从市场融资。

speaker: Unknown
en: There will come a time.
zh: 总有一天会到来。

speaker: Unknown
en: There'll be some form of a blowup, a pretty high-profile one where people lose a whole bunch of money, and that will cause a reset.
zh: 会出现某种形式的崩盘，相当高调的一次，让人们损失一大笔钱，而这会引发一次重置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the companies that are disciplined in how they spend the capital
zh: 而我认为那些在花钱方式上有纪律的公司

speaker: Unknown
en: So they have years of runway will be the survivors and the ones that have to raise money in three months will be gone.
zh: 也就是说它们有好几年的跑道，将会是幸存者，而那些三个月内就得融资的公司将会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: My advice to founders is treat every dollar as if it's your own money and spend it really carefully.
zh: 我给创始人的建议是，把每一美元都当作是你自己的钱，非常谨慎地花。

speaker: Unknown
en: And don't expect the kind of ebullient freely available capital thing to exist forever.
zh: 不要指望那种资本充裕、随手可得的环境会永远存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: So raise money now, but keep it in the bank.
zh: 所以现在就融资，但把钱存在银行里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't spend it.
zh: 别花。

speaker: Unknown
en: Or spend it judiciously.
zh: 或者审慎地花。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you see the difference between investing, which is what you've typically done in the public markets versus private markets in terms of ventures?
zh: 你怎么看投资的差别，你通常在公开市场做的投资，与风险投资意义上的私募市场投资，有什么不同？

speaker: Unknown
en: Sure.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So public markets, we're investing in what we call super durable growth companies, you know, businesses that are the most dominant companies, their respective spaces.
zh: 在公开市场，我们投资的是我们所谓的超级持久增长型公司，也就是那些在各自领域最具主导地位的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're highly profitable.
zh: 它们盈利能力很强。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have strong balance sheets.
zh: 它们资产负债表很强。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the key sort of success factor is predicting kind of their ability to continue to, you know, either gain or maintain market share and grow their business and have pricing power.
zh: 而关键的成功因素是预测它们能否持续地获得或维持市场份额、发展业务并拥有定价权。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the public markets, you know, yes, the CEO matters, but we've always had the view, well, if we don't like the CEO, we can find a better one.
zh: 在公开市场，是的，CEO 很重要，但我们一直以来的观点是，如果我们不喜欢这个 CEO，我们可以找一个更好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In venture, you're really betting on the person and more than the business plan.
zh: 在风险投资中，你真正押注的是这个人，更甚于商业计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you're investing in a company that is, you know, maybe pre-revenue or it's losing money.
zh: 而且你投资的是一家可能还没有收入或者正在亏钱的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're betting on their ability to grow at a fast enough rate that ultimately they go from being a capital consumer to one that's going to generate cash over time.
zh: 你押注的是它们能以足够快的速度增长，最终从资本消耗者转变为随着时间推移能产生现金的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has some similar elements, but it's much more founder-dependent, CEO-dependent than the public markets.
zh: 它有一些相似的要素，但比公开市场更加依赖创始人、依赖 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best public market companies, if something happens to the CEO, you can find another great person to run it.
zh: 最好的公开市场公司，如果 CEO 出了什么事，你可以找到另一个优秀的人来经营它。

speaker: Unknown
en: The best private companies, without the CEO, you probably would write it off.
zh: 最好的私营公司，没有了 CEO，你可能会直接把它勾销。

speaker: Unknown
en: How much are you weighting the idea versus the person?
zh: 你在多大程度上权衡创意与人？

speaker: Unknown
en: I weight the person more than the idea because often the original idea is not the idea that turns out to be the success.
zh: 我更看重人而不是创意，因为最初的想法往往不是最终取得成功的那个想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: The founder is going to hit a roadblock, original idea doesn't work.
zh: 创始人会碰到路障，最初的想法行不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: My most successful venture investment, I didn't like the idea.
zh: 我最成功的风险投资，我并不喜欢那个创意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Kupang, which was Bam Kim, and his business plan was to create the Groupon of South Korea.
zh: Kupang，就是 Bam Kim，他的商业计划是打造韩国版 Groupon。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even at that time, which was 2009, I thought Groupon was a really bad business model.
zh: 甚至在当时，也就是 2009 年，我就觉得 Groupon 是一个非常糟糕的商业模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: But he made a very powerful case for why South Korea was a great piece to launch an internet business, and I liked him.
zh: 但他非常有说服力地论证了为什么韩国是创办互联网生意的好地方，而且我喜欢他这个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And ultimately, he built the Amazon of South Korea, really nothing to do with the original business model.
zh: 最终，他建成了韩国的亚马逊，跟最初的商业模式几乎没有关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the most successful...
zh: 所以最成功的……

speaker: Unknown
en: You're really betting on their ability to manage through the challenges that emerge and figure out a business model over time.
zh: 你真正押注的是他们应对浮现的挑战、并随着时间推移摸索出商业模式的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: How is AI changing the investment profession?
zh: AI 正在如何改变投资这个行业？

speaker: Unknown
en: The most important thing an investor has to do is assess the risk.
zh: 投资者必须做的最重要的事情是评估风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, the value of a business is the present value of the cash generates over its life.
zh: 我的意思是，一家企业的价值是它在存续期内产生现金的现值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's life, you know, the early years of the life matter more than the later years, but you need to predict with a pretty high degree of confidence what a business is going to look like 10 years out, 20 years out, 30 years out, if you want to make a liquid long-term investment in the business.
zh: 而它的生命周期，你知道，早期的年份比后面的年份更重要，但你需要以相当高的置信度预测一家企业 10 年后、20 年后、30 年后会是什么样子，如果你想在它身上做流动性长期投资的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we look at even liquid investments that way.
zh: 而我们连流动性投资也是这样看的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to invest in something that...
zh: 你想投资于某种……

speaker: Unknown
en: If the stock market were to shut for 10 years, you're happy to own it.
zh: 如果股市关闭 10 年，你也乐意持有它。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's good discipline.
zh: 这是很好的纪律。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that you need to think through is the risk of disruption.
zh: 你需要想清楚的事情是颠覆的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: What AI has done is massively increase the risk of disruption.
zh: AI 所做的是大幅增加了颠覆的风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got to be very, very thoughtful about the businesses.
zh: 你必须对这些企业非常非常审慎地思考。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go back to Warren Buffett.
zh: 回到 Warren Buffett。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you go back and read Warren Buffett, the greatest investor of all time, he was not able to perceive the risk of disruption created by the internet, for example.
zh: 如果你回头去读沃伦·巴菲特，有史以来最伟大的投资人，他当年也没能察觉互联网所带来的颠覆风险，比如说。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, Wikipedia disrupting Worldbook.
zh: 你知道，Wikipedia 颠覆了 Worldbook。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, now we have AI.
zh: 好了，现在我们有了 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a much more complicated problem.
zh: 这是一个复杂得多的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of us are guaranteed to look foolish with one business or another that we didn't anticipate the risk of disruption because of AI.
zh: 我们所有人注定会因为某一个生意而显得愚蠢，因为我们没有预见到 AI 带来的颠覆风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: What businesses do you think become more valuable as a result of AI?
zh: ←(correction: 见下)

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually met with one of the founders of Cognition yesterday, a very interesting company.
zh: 我昨天实际上见了 Cognition 的一位创始人，这是一家非常有意思的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their software, or their AI, in effect, enables banks, big financial institutions, for example, that spend a ton of money on...
zh: 他们的软件，或者说他们的 AI，实际上能让银行、大型金融机构，比方说，那些花大量金钱在……

speaker: Unknown
en: Dealing with legacy systems because of an agglomeration of acquisitions they did over time.
zh: 处理遗留系统上的机构受益，因为他们长期以来收购累积了一堆系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: They can rewrite the COBOL into modern code and do it in a matter of days as opposed to many months.
zh: 他们可以把 COBOL 重写成现代代码，只用几天时间，而不是好几个月。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the cost to run big financial institutions is going to come down meaningfully because of AI.
zh: 我认为运营大型金融机构的成本会因为有 AI 而显著下降。

speaker: Unknown
en: Big spenders, if you will, on tech are going to bring some of that.
zh: 那些科技上的大买家，可以这么说，会从中分得一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're going to become a lot more efficient.
zh: 他们的效率会大幅提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the question is, are they going to be able to keep the profit?
zh: 现在的问题是，他们能不能保住利润？

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone's going to be forced to use the best software to run their business more efficiently and become more AI native.
zh: 每个人都会被迫使用最好的软件来更高效地运营业务，变得更 AI 原生化。

speaker: Unknown
en: The question is whether they get to keep that profit or whether the margin gets passed on to the customer.
zh: 问题在于他们是能保住那份利润，还是利润率被让渡给了客户。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a function of the nature of the business and pricing power.
zh: 这取决于生意的性质和定价权。

speaker: Unknown
en: The problem with money generally is it's commodity and banks are in the business of providing money.
zh: 货币这个生意总体上的问题在于它是大宗商品，而银行做的就是提供货币的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a complicated question.
zh: 这是个复杂的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It depends on the business.
zh: 这取决于具体的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think AI will enable the creation of many businesses that heretofore could not be created before, and AI will enable entrepreneurs, people to become entrepreneurs who have never been entrepreneurs before.
zh: 我认为 AI 将使许多以前无法创建的生意得以创建，AI 将让那些从来没有当过创业者的人成为创业者。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just even the most recent overnight release of Meta, I haven't had a chance to play around with it, but guys in the office were talking about how easy it is to use, I think it's Muse, whatever it is.
zh: 就说 Meta 最近的一夜之间的发布吧，我还没来得及玩，但办公室里的人都在讨论它用起来多么简单，我记得叫 Muse，管它叫什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, Muse.ai.
zh: 对，Muse.ai。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, how easy it is for people to now create their own agents to do stuff for them.
zh: 对，现在人们创建自己的智能体来帮他们做事是多么容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: The pace of improvement is by far the fastest of anything I've ever seen.
zh: 这种改进的速度是我见过的任何东西里最快的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you think about Microsoft in the old days, 1.0 versus 2.0, it might be a couple of years or more between updates of consequence.
zh: 如果你想当年微软，1.0 对 2.0，重要更新之间可能要隔上几年甚至更久。

speaker: Unknown
en: Here, you get an update of consequence in days.
zh: 而在这里，几天之内就有一次重要的更新。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a bit like driving a Tesla overnight, they're updating the software.
zh: 有点像开特斯拉，一夜之间软件就更新了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that scare you as an investor?
zh: 作为投资人，这会让你害怕吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm generally not frightened, so scare is probably the wrong word, but I would say you have to be very thoughtful about
zh: 我总体上是不害怕的，所以“害怕”可能是个不准确的词，但我认为你必须非常认真地去思考

speaker: Unknown
en: The moats and how wide they really are.
zh: 护栏，以及它们到底有多宽。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's the most complicated question for an investor, how to predict the risk of disruption.
zh: 对投资人来说，如何预测颠覆风险是最复杂的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Businesses that seem like the most dominant businesses in the world, there will be some that will just disappear.
zh: 那些看起来像是世界上最占主导地位的生意，其中会有一些就这么消失掉。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me tell you about the best new product that I've used in the past five years.
zh: 让我告诉你过去五年里我用过的最好的新产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the Matic Vacuum.
zh: 这东西能吸尘，能拖地，Matic 什么都会干。

speaker: Unknown
en: This thing vacuums, it mops, Matic does everything.
zh: 这个东西能吸尘,能拖地,Matic 什么都能干。

speaker: Unknown
en: Other robots bump into things, but the Matic sees things.
zh: 别的机器人会撞上东西，但 Matic 能看见东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It actually avoids the problems.
zh: 它真的能避开问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the Matic automatically adjusts between my carpeted surfaces and my hardwood floors.
zh: 而且 Matic 会在我的地毯和硬木地板之间自动调节。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's also super easy to schedule.
zh: 它还非常容易设定日程。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have it run every night while I'm in bed, and every morning I wake up to clean floors.
zh: 我让它每晚在我睡觉时运行，每天早晨醒来就是干净的地板。

speaker: Unknown
en: Messes happen, and when they do, Matic rolls into action.
zh: 脏乱总会发生，而当它发生时，Matic 就会出动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go to maticrobots.com today and put Matic to work for you.
zh: 今天就去 maticrobots.com，让 Matic 为你效劳。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ever hit 3 p.m. and feel like your brain just quit?
zh: 有没有在下午三点感觉大脑直接罢工了？

speaker: Unknown
en: For a lot of people, that's not caffeine or sleep, it's electrolytes.
zh: 对很多人来说，那不是咖啡因或睡眠的问题，是电解质的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And water alone won't fix it.
zh: 而光喝水解决不了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's why I drink Element every day after lunch.
zh: 这就是为什么我每天午饭后喝 Element。

speaker: Unknown
en: Zero sugar, no dodgy ingredients, just a real dose of sodium, potassium, and magnesium.
zh: 零糖，没有可疑的成分，只有实实在在的钠、钾和镁。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know you're all thinking electrolytes are for athletes, but you don't have to be an athlete to benefit from it.
zh: 我知道你们都在想电解质是给运动员的，但你不必是运动员也能从中受益。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it tastes great.
zh: 而且它味道很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stay sharp in the afternoon and grab a free eight count sample pack with any purchase at drinkelement.com slash TKP.
zh: 下午保持清醒，在 drinkelement.com 斜杠 TKK 任意购买即可获得免费的八份装试饮包。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's drinkelement.com slash TKP.
zh: 网址是 drinkelement.com 斜杠 TKP。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you go from I'm interested in this company to now we're writing a check for a billion dollars into it?
zh: 你是怎么从「我对这家公司感兴趣」走到「现在我们要写一张十亿美元的支票投进去」的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Usually it's not a company we just woke up and heard of.
zh: 通常它不是我们一觉醒来才听说的一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we're looking for the best businesses in the world.
zh: 我们寻找的是世界上最好的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: So over time, we kind of build this, you know, call it a library of companies that we've followed for a long period of time.
zh: 所以随着时间推移，我们基本上建立起了一个，你可以说，一个我们已经长期跟踪了很长时间的公司库。

speaker: Unknown
en: We've liked the business.
zh: 我们喜欢这个生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we haven't had a chance to own it because, you know, we may have done a lot of work, but we said, look, at this price at 35 times earnings or whatever, it's hard for us to get to a 20 plus percent rate of return, which is our ambition.
zh: 而我们一直没有机会持有它，因为，你知道，我们可能做了大量研究，但我们会说，瞧，在这个价格下，按 35 倍市盈率或随便什么倍数，我们很难达到 20% 以上的年回报率，而那是我们的目标。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we do the work and then put it aside on valuation concerns.
zh: 所以我们把研究做完，然后出于估值的顾虑先放到一边。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we wait for the day that either some macro event happens, COVID, that gives us a chance to buy that kind of a business, or even, you know, the SaaS apocalypse.
zh: 然后我们就等待那一天的到来——要么是某个宏观事件发生，比如 COVID，给了我们买入这类生意的机会，要么就是，你知道的，SaaS 末日。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, SaaS-pocalypse.
zh: 是的，SaaS-pocalypse（SaaS 末日）。

speaker: Unknown
en: Which caused, you know, pretty much everything to do with software to get repriced.
zh: 它导致基本上所有和软件相关的东西都被重新定价了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That gave us an opportunity, for example, to buy Microsoft, in our view, at a very
zh: 那给了我们一个机会，比如，以在我们看来非常

speaker: Unknown
en: Attractive Valuation and a host of other really high quality businesses.
zh: 有吸引力的估值买入了微软，以及一大批其他真正高质量的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the process is we typically have two members of the team do a deep dive on a company.
zh: 但流程通常是这样的：我们让团队的两名成员对一家公司做深度研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll start obviously with kind of the SEC filings, 10Ks, 10Qs, conference call transcripts.
zh: 他们显然会从 SEC 文件开始，10K、10Q、电话会议记录。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then we'll kind of assemble what the key issues are that we're trying to understand.
zh: 然后我们会梳理出我们试图理解的关键问题是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We spend a fair amount of time on expert networks.
zh: 我们花了相当多的时间在专家网络上。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll talk to former employees of the company.
zh: 我们会和公司的前员工交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll talk to other industry experts.
zh: 我们会和其他行业专家交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: We'll talk to people like competitors to get to the underlying issues.
zh: 我们会和竞争对手这样的人交谈，以触及底层的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then we build a model of the business and get an assessment of how does this pencil, what return does this generate at the price we can buy it for today.
zh: 然后我们会为这个生意建一个模型，评估一下这笔账算不算得过来，按我们今天能买到的价格，它能产生多少回报。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are some of the elements.
zh: 这些是其中的一些要素。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then that team will put together a deck
zh: 然后那个团队会整理出一份演示文稿

speaker: Unknown
en: And they'll present to the group.
zh: 并向全组做展示。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, that two-person team usually is not Ryan or myself.
zh: 而这个两人团队通常不是 Ryan 也不是我。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ryan's our CIO.
zh: Ryan 是我们的 CIO。

speaker: Unknown
en: I guess I'd call it the portfolio manager.
zh: 我想我算是组合经理。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we do our own sort of independent assessment, which gives us enough information to be dangerous to ask the right questions.
zh: 我们会做我们自己独立的评估，这给了我们足够的信息去「构成威胁」——也就是问出正确的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we have the balance of the team, another five people who haven't done the work in the name.
zh: 然后我们有团队的其他成员，另外五个人，他们没有对这家公司做过研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that group comes together to discuss an investment.
zh: 这个群体会聚在一起讨论这项投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: And out of that meeting may come a decision to make an investment in the company or may say, okay, there's still some open issues.
zh: 那次会议可能会得出投资这家公司的决定，也可能会说，好吧，还有一些未解决的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's get to the bottom of this concern.
zh: 让我们把这个疑虑查个水落石出。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they'll go back and do the work and come back to the team.
zh: 然后他们会回去继续研究，再回到团队这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the basic process.
zh: 这就是基本流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: How are you guys using AI internally in that investment process to either speed up the work or do work that you normally couldn't do?
zh: 你们在投资流程中是如何在内部使用 AI 的？是为了加快研究工作，还是做你们平时做不了的工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, today we're really using AI more as a research tool to learn about a certain subject that's relevant.
zh: 是的，今天我们更多是把 AI 当作一个研究工具，来学习某个相关的特定主题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It hasn't, I would say, crept too deeply into our process.
zh: 我得说，它还没有太多地渗透进我们的流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not using it to build models.
zh: 我们没有用它来建模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: In a world where everyone has the same access to AI, it's hard to be differentiated.
zh: 在一个人人都能使用同样 AI 的世界里，很难做到差异化。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, what's left to humanity is kind of the outside-the-box thinking, the creative process, the insight that's gleaned from looking at all the facts, whereas AI is a bit of a review of everything that happened before.
zh: 你知道，留给人类的，是跳出框架的思考、创造性的过程、从审视所有事实中获得的洞见，而 AI 更多是对之前发生过的一切的一种回顾。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you look at our most successful investments, they've usually been cases where we've done something that someone hasn't done before.
zh: 如果你看看我们最成功的那些投资，通常都是我们做了别人没做过的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, buying credit default swaps before, you know, a pandemic, for example, or investing in the stock of a bankrupt company or shorting the credit of a AAA company before the financial crisis.
zh: 你知道，比如在疫情之前买入信用违约互换，或者投资一家破产公司的股票，或者在金融危机之前做空一家 AAA 评级公司的信用。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are among our best investments and they were, you couldn't have found in a model, you know, AI would not have told you to do any of those things.
zh: 这些是我们最好的投资之列，而它们是你在模型里找不到的，你知道，AI 不会告诉你去做这些事情中的任何一件。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of value investors have underperformed sort of like post 2010, 2011, but you haven't.
zh: 很多价值投资者在 2010、2011 年之后表现都跑输了，但你们没有。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do you think that is?
zh: 你认为这是为什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: We've been very good about
zh: 我们一直非常擅长

speaker: Unknown
en: Continually sort of increasing our standards for business quality.
zh: 持续地提高我们对生意质量的标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to own the best businesses in the world that have a very low risk of disruption, and I think we're quite disciplined about that.
zh: 我们想持有世界上最好的那些生意，它们被颠覆的风险非常低，而我认为在这点上我们相当有纪律。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the other thing is that we're not just a long-only equity investor.
zh: 另一点是，我们不仅仅是一个只做多的股票投资者。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have opportunistically made a pile of money in a couple of cases when we've had a view about macro events that's different from others, and when you have that and you can find an asymmetric way to make that bet, you can make a lot of money.
zh: 我们曾有机会在地缘宏观事件上与别人看法不同时赚了一大笔钱,而当你有这种观点,并且能找到一种不对称的方式去下注时,你就能赚很多钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we made a lot of money kind of going into COVID because we, I would say, were weeks ahead of the world and of a few that there would have to be a global economic shutdown.
zh: 所以我们在进入新冠疫情期间赚了很多钱,因为我认为,我们比全世界早了几周意识到必然会出现全球经济停摆。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we made a lot of money because we said there has to be massive inflation.
zh: 我们还赚了很多钱,因为当时我们说必然会出现大规模通货膨胀。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we bet that rates would rise.
zh: 所以我们押注利率会上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things we did that, you know, we've talked about it before, but we had this very large loss circa 2015, 2016.
zh: 我们做过的一件事——你知道,我们以前聊过——是我们在大约 2015、2016 年有过一次非常大的亏损。

speaker: Unknown
en: And after that experience, I said, we've got to take our investment principles and literally engrave them on a stone tablet and put them on our desk.
zh: 在那次经历之后,我说,我们必须把我们的投资原则刻在一块石碑上,放在我们的办公桌上。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a very good way.
zh: 这是一种非常好的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having a checklist is actually not a bad way to make sure you avoid mistakes.
zh: 有一份检查清单其实是避免犯错的一个不错的办法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have a good checklist.
zh: 而我们有一份很好的检查清单。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's on that checklist?
zh: 清单上有什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: The nature of the businesses we're investing in, simple, predictable, free cash flow, generative companies, the kinds of management teams that we're looking for, focus on large cap, kind of liquid public companies, an aversion to short selling.
zh: 我们所投资企业的性质——简单、可预测、有自由现金流、能创造现金的公司;我们寻找的管理层类型;专注于大盘、流动性较好的上市公司;对做空的反感。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was something, a good lesson.
zh: 这是一条很好的教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: And on the asymmetric side, we're looking for a case where we have a view that's different from the rest of the world.
zh: 而在不对称性这一边,我们寻找的是我们对世界的看法与众不同的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we can express that view with an instrument where the payoff is very large relative to the amount of capital that we put to work.
zh: 然后我们可以用一种工具来表达这个观点,其回报相对于我们投入的资金量而言非常大。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, it's very simple.
zh: 但是,你知道,这非常简单。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're looking for the best super durable growth companies in the world.
zh: 我们寻找的是世界上最超级持久的成长型公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: We spend a lot of time thinking about moats.
zh: 我们花很多时间思考护城河。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, we want them run by the best teams in the world, or if it's not run by the best team in the world, we want to have someone in mind that we could install if we need to replace the team.
zh: 显然,我们希望它们由世界上最优秀的团队经营,或者如果不是由世界上最优秀的团队经营,我们要心里有一个人选,以便在需要更换团队时可以把这个人安插进去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did you stop short selling?
zh: 你们为什么停止做空?

speaker: Unknown
en: I never actually liked short selling because it's asymmetry in reverse, right?
zh: 我其实从来都不喜欢做空,因为它是反向的不对称,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You can lose infinity and your amount you can make is finite, but I was...
zh: 你可能损失无穷大,而你能赚的金额是有限的,但我当时……

speaker: Unknown
en: We shorted the bond insurers going into the financial crisis, and that was a very- That was the MBIA one?
zh: 我们在金融危机来临前做空了债券保险公司,那是一次非常——是 MBIA 那次吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, but most of the money we made, we made on the credit default swaps as opposed to shorting stock, and then we did nothing.
zh: 是的,但我们赚的大部分钱是通过信用违约互换赚的,而不是靠做空股票,然后我们就什么都不做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then someone pitched me on a fraudulent pyramid scheme, and then we did the work and said, it's a fraudulent pyramid scheme.
zh: 后来有人向我推介了一个欺诈性的金字塔骗局,我们做了功课,确认它是个欺诈性的金字塔骗局。

speaker: Unknown
en: We said, how can we lose money shorting a fraudulent pyramid scheme and then delivering to the FTC a detailed analysis?
zh: 我们说,我们怎么可能在一个做空欺诈性金字塔骗局、并向 FTC 提交详细分析的交易上亏钱呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll have to investigate, and the people being harmed are-
zh: 他们必须展开调查,而且被伤害的是——

speaker: Unknown
en: The most disadvantaged people in society.
zh: 社会中最弱势的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we thought it was an amazing setup.
zh: 所以我们认为这是一个绝妙的布局。

speaker: Unknown
en: We like to make investments where the wind is at our back.
zh: 我们喜欢做顺风的投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we said, look, the wind's at our back.
zh: 而我们说,瞧,这绝对是顺风。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're helping a group of disadvantaged people are being taken advantage of.
zh: 我们在帮助一群正被剥削的弱势人群。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an evil company.
zh: 这是一家邪恶的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: This has to work.
zh: 这必须成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we underestimated the risk of
zh: 而我们低估了

speaker: Unknown
en: Market dynamics, i.e.
zh: 市场动态的风险,也就是说

speaker: Unknown
en: Carl Icahn showing up, buying the stock, putting capital to work against us, and it just reminded us that it's a really shitty business.
zh: Carl Icahn 出现了,买入股票,投入资本与我们作对,这只是提醒了我们,做空真是一门非常糟糕的生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: The company that you were, they're shorting the pyramid scheme, we won't mention the name, but that generated these huge attacks against you.
zh: 那家公司——你们做空那个金字塔骗局的那家,我们不提名字——对你们发起了大规模攻击。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was websites against you.
zh: 有专门针对你们的网站。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a famous CNBC segment that I think came as a result of that.
zh: 还有一段著名的 CNBC 节目,我想就是由此而来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Was that?
zh: 是那样吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: What about the personal cost to you when you're willing to put out a contrary opinion like that?
zh: 当你愿意公开表达这样的反对意见时,你个人付出的代价是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, it's much easier to be an investor in companies.
zh: 嗯,做多公司要容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: You make a lot more friends, right?
zh: 你能交到更多朋友,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: You buy a stock, other people pile in with you, it goes up, everyone wins.
zh: 你买一只股票,别人跟风买入,股价上涨,大家都赢。

speaker: Unknown
en: You short a stock, and in that case, we were the vast majority of the short interest, so everyone else was sort of on the other side.
zh: 你做空一只股票——在那个案例里,我们是空头持仓的绝大多数,所以其他所有人几乎都在对立面。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then you had a company that we were an existential threat to.
zh: 然后你还面对一家被我们构成生存威胁的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were willing to use whatever they had been attacked over time by critics, by media, by otherwise.
zh: 他们愿意动用他们所拥有的一切——他们长期以来一直受到批评者、媒体和其他人的攻击。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they built up a lot of infrastructure to go after the critics.
zh: 而他们建立了很多基础设施来对付批评者。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they were kind of well prepared to kind of go after us.
zh: 所以他们某种程度上已经做好了充分准备来对付我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it became a bit of a hedge fund trade where let's go squeeze Bill.
zh: 然后它变成了有点像对冲基金的交易:来吧,我们去轧空 Bill。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was kind of the unfortunate part of it where, you know, in some sense, the industry is like, okay, these guys are over their skis.
zh: 这就是其中比较不幸的部分，你知道，从某种意义上说，业界的态度是，好吧，这些人玩得太过火了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We can squeeze them out.
zh: 我们可以把他们挤出去。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was not the fun part.
zh: 这可不是什么有趣的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: You were relatively quiet, I would say, from a public life point of view compared to what you were before.
zh: 从公开生活的角度来说，比起你以前，你相对安静，我可以这么说。

speaker: Unknown
en: And now in the last few years, you've been a lot more vocal.
zh: 而现在，在最近几年里，你的发声多了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why now?
zh: 为什么是现在？

speaker: Unknown
en: I've always been kind of a free speech kind of thing.
zh: 我一直是个崇尚言论自由的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Go back to my high school yearbook.
zh: 翻回我高中的毕业纪念册。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was listed as most verbose.
zh: 我被列为「最健谈」。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my yearbook epithet was a closed mouth gathers no foot.
zh: 而且我的纪念册题词是「闭嘴不集脚」。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was sort of known for being expressive about my point of view.
zh: 所以我算是以善于表达自己观点而闻名的。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of my important drivers in life was I always wanted to be able to say what I believed.
zh: 我人生中重要的驱动力之一，就是我始终希望能够说出我所相信的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: As my follower count grew on Twitter, it gave me on the margin more influence.
zh: 随着我在 Twitter 上的粉丝数增长，这在边际上给了我更多的影响力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as I cared about various issues, I wanted to help advance the narrative.
zh: 而因为我关心各种议题，我想要帮助推进叙事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's why I've been more public about it.
zh: 这就是为什么我在公开场合更加发声。 [[555→565]] 被它奏效所回报，从小事开始，你真的可以用一条推文影响政府和历史进程，这相当酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rewarded by it working, beginning with smaller things, and you can actually influence the administration in the course of history with a tweet, which is pretty cool.
zh: 因为它成功运行而获得回报,从小事开始,而且你实际上可以通过一条推文影响行政过程中的历史进程,这非常酷。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of evil can go by if no one's willing to say the emperor's not wearing clothes or more.
zh: 如果没有人愿意说皇帝没穿衣服或者更多的话，很多恶事就会悄悄溜过去。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to come back just one second to the AI thing for a move on for a minute.
zh: 我想回到 AI 那个话题一秒钟，然后再往前走一分钟。

speaker: Unknown
en: How are you using that personally?
zh: 你个人是怎么使用它的？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm using it a lot more recently.
zh: 我最近用得多了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, my daughter's had a major health incident, and AI is amazing at, you know, vetting, helping you make medical decisions for a child.
zh: 你知道，我女儿出了一次严重的健康事故，而 AI 在帮你为孩子的医疗决策把关方面非常了不起。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an incredibly powerful tool.
zh: 它是一个极其强大的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think every doctor should actually be checking their work with, you know, Dr. Claude, or pick your favorite website, make your favorite AI.
zh: 而且我认为每个医生都应该用，你知道的，Claude 医生，或者选你最喜欢的网站，选你最喜欢的 AI，来核对他们自己的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think companies like Brookfield get more valuable where it's like a tangible almost infrastructure becomes more valuable in a world of AI?
zh: 你认为像 Brookfield 这样的公司会不会变得更有价值，就是说在 AI 的世界里，这种有形的、几乎基础设施式的东西会变得更有价值？

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's another bet, and I'd love to hear your reaction to this, which is sort of Thrive is starting to buy these sports teams under the assumption that we have this barbell, right?
zh: 还有另一个赌注，我很想听听你的反应，就是 Thrive 开始在这些假设下收购体育球队，即我们有一个杠铃结构，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We have AI in one hand, and on the other hand, these tangible experiences are going to become more and more meaningful to people, and presumably they'll pay more for those experiences.
zh: 我们一只手握着 AI，另一只手，这些有形的体验会变得越来越对人们有意义，而且想必他们会为这些体验支付更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So on Brookfield, I think it's an incredibly well-run, amazing company.
zh: 至于 Brookfield，我认为它是一家运营得极其出色、了不起的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're very good at infrastructure and they're very good at financing.
zh: 他们非常擅长基础设施，而且非常擅长融资。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're very good at building things.
zh: 他们非常擅长建造东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So think data centers, think power.
zh: 想想数据中心，想想电力。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's effectively infinite demand for compute and they're very well positioned.
zh: 对算力的需求实际上是无限的，而他们的位置非常有利。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think Brookfield is an AI winner for sure.
zh: 所以我认为 Brookfield 肯定是一个 AI 赢家。

speaker: Unknown
en: They'll provide a lot of the backbone power and otherwise.
zh: 他们会提供很多骨干电力之类的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I'm a big Josh Kushner fan.
zh: 是的，我是 Josh Kushner 的忠实粉丝。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know how much of the recent baseball investment is Thrive-related or personal.
zh: 我不知道最近的棒球投资有多少与 Thrive 有关，还是个人行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not quite clear to me, but I do think that there's a lot of people sitting home being lonely, but you go to a big sport event, the feeling that you have at a Knicks game.
zh: 这对我来说不太清楚，但我确实认为有很多人坐在家里感到孤独，而当你去参加一场大型体育赛事时，那种你在尼克斯比赛中的感受。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe at the end of the game, half the crowd is unhappy.
zh: 也许在比赛结束时，一半的观众是不高兴的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But while it's underway, it's sort of a very human elation type experience.
zh: 但在比赛进行期间，那是一种非常人性化的狂喜式体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, I don't know that baseball teams are
zh: 现在，我不知道棒球队是不是

speaker: Unknown
en: They're not valued in a way that I think about valuing most assets.
zh: 它们的估值方式与我对大多数资产的估值思考方式不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they're valued more like an artwork than a financial enterprise.
zh: 我认为它们的估值更像一件艺术品，而不是一个金融企业。

speaker: Unknown
en: The vast number of sports teams, as far as I know, if they make money, it's not a lot.
zh: 据我所知，绝大多数体育球队，即便赚钱，也赚不了多少。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not like the owner is expecting them to generate massive cash.
zh: 而且老板并不指望它们产生巨额现金。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're taking a small return today on the basis that it's going to generate a lot more cash flow in the future.
zh: 他们今天接受较小的回报，基础是未来会产生更多的现金流。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would think the vast majority of sports owners are prepared to spend every dollar that they're allowed to in expanding their franchise.
zh: 我会认为绝大多数体育球队老板都准备把他们被允许花费的每一块钱都花在扩张他们的球队上。

speaker: Unknown
en: Are you going to buy a sports team?
zh: 你会去买一支体育球队吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: No.
zh: 不会。

speaker: Unknown
en: You went from being an occasionally loud activist to trying to enact change behind the scenes.
zh: 你从一个偶尔大声的活动家，变成了试图在幕后推动变革的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why the change?
zh: 为什么会有这个转变？

speaker: Unknown
en: And is it more effective this way?
zh: 而且这样更有效吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's because we were able to effectuate change behind the scenes and we weren't when we started, right?
zh: 这是因为我们能够在幕后促成改变,而我们刚开始的时候做不到,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: When we went into the business, we didn't have credibility or reputation.
zh: 我们刚进入这个行业时,没有信誉或声望。

speaker: Unknown
en: We hadn't been in the boardroom.
zh: 我们没进过董事会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was 20, you know, 20 plus years younger.
zh: 我当时年轻,你知道,年轻二十多岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in that world where you have limited financial resources, you have limited reputational resources, you can buy 5% of a company and you have to win on the power of the idea to get the big institutions to support you.
zh: 在那个你财力有限、声望资源有限的世界里,你可以买下一家公司 5% 的股份,但你必须靠想法本身的力量来赢得大型机构的支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might have to end up in a proxy contest, et cetera.
zh: 你可能最终还得打代理权争夺战,等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Twenty years later, I've been on multiple boards, as I have other members of the team.
zh: 二十年过去了,我在多个董事会任职过,我们团队的其他成员也一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a track record of success of investing in a company, being a long-term investor.
zh: 我们有投资一家公司并成为长期投资者的成功记录。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the early days, they would say, oh, you're just a short-term investor.
zh: 在早期,他们会说,哦,你们只是个短期投资者。

speaker: Unknown
